data.narrative:
Genesis AI, a seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Zhou Xian, Theophile Gervet, and Tsun-Hsuan Wang, has raised $105M to date. The target operates within a sector containing nine comparable entities—one public (277810.KQ) and eight private firms including Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, and Generalist AI—though peers at identical stage and valuation tier remain sparse.

Stage-progression methodology is applicable here, using the $105M total raised as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.5x multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage advancement in this sector. This yields a point estimate of $262M. Peer-median triangulation could not be executed; while ten same-sector comparables exist, insufficient datapoints survived filtering for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier cohorts (minimum three required), making a narrow peer analysis unreliable without introducing sector-wide median bias.

The valuation analysis supports a range of $223M (low) to $302M (high), centered on $262M. This single-method reliance introduces material uncertainty around terminal value assumptions embedded in the stage-progression multiplier. Key risks include genesis stage-specific burn dynamics, manufacturing capital requirements, and the sparsity of direct peer benchmarks. Validation through additional methods—transaction comps or DCF—would strengthen conviction, but currently unavailable data precludes their application.
